rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation on four real skeletons (which recalibrated the single-leader test before the real run), 46 replication units in three embedding variants, four natives (G26, G35, G44, G12), scorecard, 582 estimates rows, confirmatory script frozen and dry-run. Holdout not run.
rationale.faithfulness: Within-agent role contrasts are calibrated (null 0-0.15) and replicate across embedding variants for the reply channel; the content contrasts are noisy and one is model-dependent. The router model fails; the attention-only rival fits two natives and the source rival one. Scorecard all 1s except I.
rationale.usefulness: A practical negative for operators: installing or electing a leader buys replies, not aggregation or relay of content. The reply premium (+0.4 replies per statement) is a usable number; the elected-leader-as-source finding rests on one leader.

one_line: Designated leaders get about 0.4 more replies per statement but absorb and relay no more content; the elected leader is a content source.

models.note: Leaders are not sink nodes of the directed content coupling
Inflow tracks answering; leader role adds attention only

v2.claim: Designated leaders are attention hubs (+0.39 to +0.45 replies per statement), not content routers; attention is unaligned with content flow (D_p −0.04); the one elected leader (#26) is a content source
v2.scope: 46 units; natives G26, G35, G44, G12

ladder.factor: synthetic identification (single-leader calls calibrated on skeleton nulls)

v2.decision: route through people who answer, not through designated leaders

raters.claim: Designated leaders and judges gain attention (+0.39 and +0.45 agent replies per statement on-role, p <= 0.007) but are not content routers: no strong-router rise in read-gated inflow (chi x2 with outflow x0.2, where within-agent power is 1.0) in #35 or #12; the elected #26 leader is a source instead.

partial replication: 2 powered within-agent natives, #26 and #44 consistent; < 6 units
